metadata.title: Optimization by Simulated Annealing
metadata.authors: S. Kirkpatrick, C. D. Gelatt Jr., M. P. Vecchi
metadata.source_note: Extracted from PDF->text fallback; .tex source not available. Math fidelity reduced.

nodes.name: Combinatorial optimization problem
nodes.statement: A problem of finding minimum or maximum values of a cost (objective) function $f(\{x_i\})$ of very many independent variables, representing a quantitative measure of the goodness of some complex system.
nodes.statement_clean: A combinatorial optimization problem seeks to minimize or maximize a cost function over a discrete configuration space.

nodes.name: Traveling Salesman Problem (TSP)
nodes.statement: Given a list of $N$ cities and a means of calculating the cost of traveling between any two cities, plan a route passing through each city once and returning to the starting point that minimizes the total cost.
nodes.statement_clean: TSP asks for the minimum-cost Hamiltonian tour through N cities.

nodes.name: NP-complete problem class
nodes.statement: The class of problems for which no exact-solution method with computing effort bounded by a power of $N$ has been found, and where a polynomial-time solution to one would yield polynomial-time solutions for all members.
nodes.statement_clean: NP-complete problems are computationally intractable in the worst case but reducible to one another.
nodes.origin_citation: Garey and Johnson, Computers and Intractability (1979)

nodes.name: Iterative improvement
nodes.statement: A heuristic that starts from a known configuration, applies a standard rearrangement operation to all parts of the system in turn, and only accepts rearrangements that improve the cost function until no further improvements can be found.
nodes.statement_clean: Iterative improvement performs greedy local search, accepting only downhill moves.

nodes.name: Boltzmann distribution
nodes.statement: In thermal equilibrium at temperature $T$, each configuration with energy $E(\{r_i\})$ is weighted by its Boltzmann probability factor $\exp(-E(\{r_i\})/k_B T)$, where $k_B$ is Boltzmann's constant.
nodes.statement_clean: In thermal equilibrium, configuration probabilities follow the Boltzmann weighting in energy and temperature.

nodes.name: Partition function
nodes.statement: The generating function $Z = \mathrm{Tr}\,\exp(-E/k_B T)$, where $\mathrm{Tr}$ denotes a sum over all possible configurations of the atoms in the sample system.
nodes.statement_clean: The partition function sums Boltzmann weights over all configurations.

nodes.name: Free energy, entropy, specific heat
nodes.statement: Free energy $F(T) = -k_B T \log Z$ encodes ensemble averages: average energy $\langle E(T)\rangle$, entropy $S(T)$ (logarithm of contributing configurations), and specific heat $C(T) = d\langle E\rangle/dT$ measuring typical energy fluctuations.
nodes.statement_clean: Free energy, entropy, and specific heat are derived from the partition function and characterize the ensemble.

nodes.name: Effective temperature for optimization
nodes.statement: An effective temperature $T$, in the same units as the cost function, used as a control parameter to weight uphill moves in optimization via $\exp(-\Delta f / T)$.
nodes.statement_clean: The effective temperature is a control parameter in optimization, played by analogy to physical temperature.

nodes.name: Simulated annealing
nodes.statement: An optimization process consisting of first 'melting' the system at a high effective temperature, then lowering the temperature by slow stages until the system 'freezes' and no further changes occur.
nodes.statement_clean: Simulated annealing iteratively samples configurations while gradually reducing an effective temperature.

nodes.name: Annealing schedule
nodes.statement: The chosen sequence of temperatures together with the number of rearrangements of $\{x_i\}$ attempted to reach equilibrium at each temperature.
nodes.statement_clean: An annealing schedule prescribes the cooling rate and equilibration effort at each temperature.

nodes.name: Frustration / spin glass
nodes.statement: A system in which interactions favoring different and incompatible kinds of ordering are simultaneously present; spin glasses are magnetic alloys exhibiting competition between ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic ordering.
nodes.statement_clean: Frustration arises when no configuration can satisfy all competing interactions; spin glasses are the canonical example.

nodes.name: Metropolis algorithm
nodes.statement: Monte Carlo procedure that simulates a system in equilibrium at temperature $T$ by accepting random moves with probability $\min(1, \exp(-\Delta E / k_B T))$.
nodes.statement_clean: The Metropolis algorithm samples Boltzmann-distributed configurations via accept/reject Monte Carlo moves.
output: Sequence of configurations approximately distributed as $\exp(-E/k_B T)/Z$
nodes.pseudocode: Repeat: (1) propose a small random displacement and compute $\Delta E$; (2) if $\Delta E \leq 0$ accept; (3) else accept with probability $P(\Delta E) = \exp(-\Delta E / k_B T)$ by drawing a uniform random number in $(0,1)$ and comparing to $P(\Delta E)$.
nodes.origin_citation: Metropolis, Rosenbluth, Rosenbluth, Teller, Teller (J. Chem. Phys. 1953)

nodes.name: Simulated annealing algorithm
nodes.statement: Apply the Metropolis algorithm with the cost function in place of energy, starting at a high effective temperature and cooling through an annealing schedule until the system freezes.
nodes.statement_clean: Simulated annealing applies Metropolis sampling to a combinatorial cost function while gradually cooling.
input: Concise description of a configuration of the system
Annealing schedule (temperatures and lengths of equilibration)
output: A near-optimal (low cost) configuration found at the freezing temperature
nodes.pseudocode: Initialize $T \gets T_0$ (high). While not frozen: (i) at temperature $T$, run Metropolis until equilibrium (a target number of accepted moves per element, or an attempt cap); (ii) lower $T$ according to schedule (e.g. $T_{n+1} = (T_1/T_0) T_n$ with ratio $0.9$). Stop when no further changes occur over several successive temperatures.

nodes.name: Metropolis acceptance probability
nodes.statement: $P(\Delta E) = \exp(-\Delta E / k_B T)$ for $\Delta E > 0$; configurations with $\Delta E \leq 0$ are always accepted.

nodes.name: Entropy from specific heat
nodes.statement: $S(T) = S(T_1) + \int_{T_1}^{T} \frac{C(T')}{T'} dT'$, recovering entropy by integrating the specific heat from a reference temperature $T_1$ at which $S$ is known.

nodes.name: Two-way chip partition problem
nodes.statement: Partition $N$ circuits between two chips to minimize the objective $f = \sum_{i,j}(a_{ij}/4)(\mu_i - \mu_j)^2 + \lambda(\sum_i \mu_i)^2$, where $a_{ij}$ are connectivity counts, $\mu_i = \pm 1$ indicates chip assignment, and $\lambda$ balances boundary crossings against imbalance.
nodes.statement_clean: Assign circuits to two chips so as to minimize boundary signal crossings while keeping the chips balanced.

nodes.name: Partition objective as spin-glass Hamiltonian
nodes.statement: $f = \sum_{i,j}(a_{ij}/4)(\mu_i - \mu_j)^2 + \lambda \big(\sum_i \mu_i\big)^2$, with the recommended balance weight $\lambda \sim z/2$ where $z$ is the average circuit fan-in plus fan-out.

nodes.name: Spin-glass nature of partition objective
nodes.statement: The partition objective $f$ has the form of a spin-glass Hamiltonian; for uncorrelated $a_{ij}$ the system has a spin-glass phase at low temperatures with many nearly degenerate ground states of nearly equal energy and no obvious symmetry.
nodes.statement_clean: The two-way partition cost behaves like a frustrated spin glass with many near-optimal ground states.
conclusions: Significant improvement over random partitions is possible
It is not very fruitful to search for the absolute optimum
nodes.notes: Stated as a qualitative implication of the spin-glass analogy (cited Sherrington-Kirkpatrick 1975).

nodes.name: IBM 370 microprocessor two-way partition
nodes.statement: A logic design for an IBM 370 microprocessor with about 5000 primitive gates and 200 external signals is partitioned onto two chips. Random assignment requires ~3000 pins per chip; simulated annealing yields chips needing 353 and 321 pins; rapid quench (T=0) yields 677-730 pins per chip.
nodes.statement_clean: Simulated annealing dramatically reduces the pin count needed for a two-chip partition of an IBM 370 microprocessor.

nodes.name: Chip placement problem
nodes.statement: Assign chips to physical positions on a multichip module so as to minimize signal propagation distance and wiring congestion, subject to wireability constraints.
nodes.statement_clean: Assign chips to module positions to minimize wire length and avoid wiring congestion.

nodes.name: Net-crossing histogram
nodes.statement: For a set of natural boundaries between rows or columns of chip sites, the histogram whose entries count the number of nets crossing each boundary; the sum of entries in the horizontal (resp. vertical) histogram lower-bounds the total horizontal (resp. vertical) wire length.
nodes.statement_clean: The net-crossing histogram counts wires crossing each boundary and lower-bounds wire length.

nodes.name: 98-chip IBM 3081 ceramic module placement
nodes.statement: Ninety-eight chips on a 10x10 ceramic module of the IBM 3081 are placed by simulated annealing using random pairwise interchanges; histogram peaks decrease ~30% and total estimated wire length ~10% versus the original layout, in 250,000 attempts (12 minutes on an IBM 3033).
nodes.statement_clean: Annealing reduces wire-crossing peaks by ~30% on the IBM 3081 98-chip module.

nodes.name: Specific heat as freezing indicator
nodes.statement: A maximum in the specific heat $C(T)$ signals a change in the state of order; in optimization, large $C$ indicates that freezing has begun, that very slow cooling is required, and identifies temperature ranges where important rearrangements occur.

nodes.name: Global wire routing problem
nodes.statement: Route wires connecting placed circuits along links of a grid so as to minimize total wire length and number of bends while spreading the wire as evenly as possible across links to avoid overflowing link capacity.
nodes.statement_clean: Assign each connection a path along grid links to minimize length and balance link congestion.

nodes.name: Wiring objective F
Wiring objective as random spin-glass Hamiltonian
nodes.statement: Substituting the L-move parametrization $\mu_i = \pm 1$ for the orientation of connection $i$, $F$ takes the form $F = \sum_i h_i \mu_i + \sum_{ij} J_{ij} \mu_i \mu_j + \text{const}$, mirroring the Hamiltonian for a random magnetic alloy or spin glass; both $J_{ij}$ and $h_i$ vanish on average so fluctuations control low-energy states.

nodes.name: 98-chip module wire routing
nodes.statement: Routing for the 98-chip module is studied with random L-orientation, alignment along $h_i$ followed by zero-T cooling, simulated annealing with L-moves, and annealing with Z-moves; Z-move annealing reduces the maximum wires per link from 173 (x) and 143 (y) to 105 (x) and 96 (y), a 57% improvement over random.
nodes.statement_clean: Z-move annealing improves the random wiring by 57% for the 98-chip module.

nodes.name: L-shaped and Z-shaped wire moves
nodes.statement: Length-preserving rearrangements of a single connection: an L-move keeps only essential bends (one per connection), while a Z-move introduces one extra bend, both keeping the total wire length minimal.

nodes.name: Clustered 400-city traveling salesman problem
nodes.statement: Four hundred cities uniformly distributed in nine regions are annealed using Lin-Kernighan subsequence-reversal moves; long inter-region steps are eliminated by $T = 0.8$ and step lengths $\alpha$ decrease from 2.0567 ($T=1.2$) to 0.7839 ($T=0$).
nodes.statement_clean: Annealing on a 400-city clustered TSP separates coarse inter-region structure from local refinements.

nodes.name: Greedy nearest-neighbor TSP heuristic
nodes.statement: From each city, go to the nearest city not already on the tour; from the $N$th city, return directly to the first.
input: Set of $N$ cities with pairwise distances
output: A tour visiting each city once
nodes.pseudocode: Pick a start city. Repeat: from the current city, move to the nearest unvisited city. After visiting all $N$ cities, return to the start.

nodes.name: Lin-Kernighan subsequence-reversal moves
nodes.statement: A move set for the TSP in which each move reverses the direction in which a section of the tour is traversed.
input: Current tour as a permutation of $1$ to $N$
output: Modified tour after a 2-opt-style segment reversal
nodes.pseudocode: Pick two positions $i < j$ in the tour. Reverse the order of cities between positions $i$ and $j$ (a 2-opt move).

nodes.name: Adaptive divide-and-conquer of annealing on TSP
nodes.statement: On a clustered TSP, simulated annealing fixes the coarse arrangement of long inter-cluster steps at intermediate temperatures (around $T = 0.8$) and refines the fine local structure within clusters at lower temperatures, with subsequence-reversal moves sufficing.
nodes.statement_clean: Annealing handles coarse structure first and fine structure later, providing an adaptive divide-and-conquer.
conclusions: Local within-cluster structure continues to evolve below $T = 0.4$

nodes.name: Four ingredients of simulated annealing
nodes.statement: Implementing simulated annealing requires four ingredients: a concise description of a configuration; a random generator of moves; a quantitative objective function; and an annealing schedule of temperatures and equilibration lengths.

nodes.name: Scaling and applicability
nodes.statement: Numerical studies suggest good-quality results with annealing schedules where computational effort scales as $N$ or as a small power of $N$, indicating broad applicability of simulated annealing as a heuristic.

nodes.name: Spin-glass perspective on optimization
nodes.statement: The connection with statistical mechanics and spin-glass models gives insight into the ease or difficulty of finding heuristic solutions and provides a more discriminating classification than the blanket NP-complete worst-case assignment.
